docTitle: Free tuition in Europe? 9 countries for Nigerian students (LinkedIn)

slides.title:
Free tuition
in *Europe*?
slides.sub: Year one added up for five countries, and what decides the price in the rest.
slides.sticker:
*But you must show
€11,904 a year in the bank

slides.title:
When I say *cheap*
I mean two numbers
slides.body: Tuition, and the proof of funds. That's the money you show the embassy to prove you can live there while you study.
slides.body2: On every slide, the red label is the proof of funds, the number people forget.

slides.title: Germany
slides.body: Most public universities don't charge tuition. For the visa you show 992 euros for every month, usually in a blocked account.
slides.work: That's €11,904 for a year, plus a small semester fee at your university.

slides.title: France
slides.body: For students from outside the EU, a master's is 3,950 euros a year. The proof of funds went up on 1 August 2026.
slides.work: That's €10,530 for a year. It used to be €7,380.

slides.title: Austria
slides.body: Nigeria isn't on the no-fee list. The proof of funds depends on your age.

slides.title:
Estonia,
where I study
slides.body: I pay 6,000 euros a year for HCI at Tallinn University. Most master's there are 4,000 to 5,200.

slides.body: My sums: the cheapest master's I found in each country plus 12 months of proof of funds. Black rows are over €14,000. Germany's semester fee is not in it.

slides.body2: And don't forget rent. If you're schooling in a city like Paris, rent is going to choke you.
